lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: similarity as a sequence of transformations
lessonRef.title: Assessment preparation: similarity as a sequence of transformations

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-2, -5) about the origin with scale factor 3. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 7 becomes a side of length 21. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 1/3; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 3
scale factor 14; the area is multiplied by 9

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 34° and ∠B = 100°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 34° and ∠E = 100°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by SSS similarity.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a segment not through the centre, under a dilation with scale factor k …
choices: is mapped to a parallel segment k times as long
is mapped to a segment k² times as long
is mapped to a segment of the same length
is mapped to a perpendicular segment k times as long

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-1, -6) about the origin with scale factor 3. Give the image.
A figure is dilated so that a side of length 2 becomes a side of length 10. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 1/5; the area is multiplied by 25
scale factor 5; the area is multiplied by 25
scale factor 5; the area is multiplied by 5
scale factor 8; the area is multiplied by 25

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 26° and ∠B = 39°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 26° and ∠E = 39°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped onto itself
is mapped to a parallel line
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped to a line with slope multiplied by the scale factor
